Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

One Business Number, Several Accounts Under It

A corporation has one nine-digit Business Number, and each kind of tax sits under it as its own programme account: corporation income tax, GST/HST, payroll. They are separate filings with separate deadlines, and closing one does nothing to the others.

That is why a corporation can be dormant for years and still be behind on more than the T2. An account nobody remembers opening is still open until it is closed.

What the T2 Needs

A T2 is transmitted against the corporation income tax account, so the Business Number has to be known before anything can be filed. It appears on any notice of assessment, in My Business Account, and on the corporation’s registration documents.

The fee of $300.00 plus HST per tax year covers the nil T2. It does not cover a GST/HST return or a payroll remittance, which is what the rows above separate out.

Closing an Account You No Longer Need

Form RC145 closes a Business Number programme account, once that account has its own final return or remittance in. An account left open can still draw correspondence after the corporation itself is gone, which is the usual reason a closed-down corporation keeps hearing from the Canada Revenue Agency.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can a T2 Be Filed Without the Business Number?

No. The return is transmitted against the corporation income tax account under that number, so it has to be known first.

Does Closing the GST/HST Account Close the T2 Obligation?

No. Each programme account is separate. The T2 is due for every tax year until the corporation is formally dissolved, whatever happens to the other accounts.

What If I Am Not Sure Whether an Account Is Open?

My Business Account lists the programme accounts on record. Answer yes here only where you know, and treat the result as the list to confirm rather than a statement of your account.

Is a Nil GST/HST Return Really Needed on a Dormant Corporation?

An open account still has its own filing obligation, nil or not. The GST/HST nil filing checker covers that account on its own.

Does the Fee Cover Any of the Other Accounts?

No. $300.00 plus HST per tax year covers one nil T2 for one corporation for one tax year. Every other account is a separate filing.

Last reviewed: October 26, 2026

Four questions about how the corporation is registered

Answer all four and the list of filings appears here.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

The Nil T2 Is One Filing, Not All of Them

A nil T2 reports the corporation’s tax year to the Canada Revenue Agency. It is not the only thing an inactive corporation owes, and the fee covers the T2 alone.

A nil T2 does not cover an Ontario annual return through the Ontario Business Registry, a federal Corporations Canada annual return at $12.00 due within 60 days of the anniversary, an Alberta AT1, a Quebec CO-17, or a nil GST/HST or payroll filing. We tell you which of these you still owe.

Two Different Bodies

Registry filings and tax returns go to different places. The annual return goes to the registry the corporation was incorporated or registered with, federally through Corporations Canada or provincially. The T2 and the programme account returns go to the Canada Revenue Agency.

Missing the registry one is what eventually dissolves a corporation without its owner intending it, which is a separate problem from an unfiled T2.

What the Fee Covers

$300.00 plus HST per tax year covers one nil T2 for one corporation for one tax year, including the T2 Short where the corporation qualifies, the GIFI schedules where they are required, your Form T183CORP package, CPA review, electronic transmission by a registered EFILE electronic filer, and your CRA confirmation emailed within 3 business days.

The $12.00 federal annual return fee is a government fee and tax does not apply to it. It is paid to Corporations Canada, not to us.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the Annual Return the Same as the T2?

No. They go to different bodies and have different deadlines. The annual return keeps the corporation on the registry; the T2 reports its tax year to the Canada Revenue Agency.

Do You File the Ontario Annual Return?

No. It is filed separately through the Ontario Business Registry and is not covered by the fee. We tell you that you owe it.

What About an Alberta AT1 or a Quebec CO-17?

Both are separate provincial returns and neither is included in the fee for the nil T2.

The Corporation Has Been Inactive for Years. Does All of This Apply to Every Year?

The T2 does: one return per tax year until dissolution. Use the unfiled years checker to list the years. The other filings follow their own cycles.

Is It Cheaper to Just Dissolve the Corporation?

Dissolving does not remove the returns already outstanding. The dissolution readiness checker sets out the order the steps run in.

content:

Side-by-side comparisonNames what pushed it overFour questionsRoutes a full return

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Last reviewed: October 26, 2026

Four questions about what happened in the tax year

Answer all four and the answer appears here.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

Where the Line Sits

A nil return and a full return are the same form. What differs is whether anything happened in the tax year. One revenue entry, one expense, one dividend or one disposal and the year is a full return, however small the amount.

Existing is not activity. A corporation can hold a bank account, own assets and stay registered for years without carrying on business, and every one of those years is nil.

What Changes When It Is Not Nil

The schedules grow with the activity, the figures stop being zero, and the work is no longer a fixed-fee filing. That is why a full return is handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca rather than here.

A holding corporation with investment income, a rental corporation and a corporation that paid or received a dividend are not nil. Those are handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

This Tool and the Dormant Test

This one compares the two kinds of return and names which applies. The dormant corporation test asks ten activity questions and names the single item that disqualifies a year, which is the finer instrument of the two. Use this to understand the difference, that one to settle a close case.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is a Nil Return a Shorter Form?

No. It is a complete T2 with the figures at zero. The identification, the fiscal year dates and the GIFI schedules where they are required are all still part of it.

Does One Small Expense Really Make It a Full Return?

Yes. There is no threshold below which activity is ignored. A single bank charge paid from the corporate account is activity.

What If Different Years Are Different?

Each tax year is judged on its own. A corporation can file nil for three years, full for one, and nil again after it.

Is the T2 Short the Same as a Nil Return?

No. The T2 Short is a shorter version of the form that some corporations qualify to use. The T2 Short eligibility checker runs all eight conditions.

What Happens If We File Nil and It Turns Out Not to Be?

We check before you pay. If we find it afterwards, we refund you in full and the work moves to gondaliyacpa.ca.

title: Nil T2 Document Checklist | What Goes Into the Return
content:
Checklist Tool

Nil T2 Document Checklist

Four questions that build the list of what actually goes into your nil T2, schedule by schedule, all of it inside the fee.

Built from four answersSchedule by scheduleNo audited statementsEverything inside the fee

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 26, 2026

Four questions about the return

Answer all four and the checklist appears here.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

Two Things Are Always Needed

Every nil T2 needs the corporation identified, which is its name, its Business Number and the fiscal year dates for the year being filed, and it needs Form T183CORP signed before the return is transmitted.

Everything else on the list depends on what the corporation holds and whether this is its first return.

Why GIFI Turns Up on a Nil Return

The most misunderstood part of a nil return is that it still carries GIFI schedules. Any one of share capital, cash, a shareholder loan, an incorporation cost or a bank charge makes Schedules 100, 125 and 141 all required, and a corporation with shares issued has share capital.

The GIFI schedule requirement checker runs those five triggers one by one.

What You Do Not Need

No audited financial statements. No bookkeeping for a year with no transactions. No appointment. The whole return is built from the answers on the form and the schedules the corporation’s own position requires, and all of it is inside $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I Need Financial Statements?

No audited statements. The return still carries the GIFI schedules where they are required, showing zero, which is a different thing from a set of prepared statements.

What Is Form T183CORP?

It is the form by which a signing officer authorises the electronic transmission of the return. It is signed on a secure single-use screen before we transmit, and it is included in the fee.

Does a First Return Need Anything Extra?

Schedule 24 is required on the first return after incorporation. The Schedule 24 first return checker confirms it.

How Is the 10% Shareholder Threshold Measured?

Schedule 50 is needed for any shareholder at 10% or more. The Schedule 50 shareholder threshold checker takes the percentages and says which shareholders are in.

Is Anything on the List Charged Separately?

No. $300.00 plus HST per tax year covers every schedule the return requires, the T183CORP package, CPA review and transmission.

Due Date Weekend and Holiday Shift Calculator

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 26, 2026

Your due date

Enter a due date and the shift appears here.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

A Due Date on a Closed Day Moves Forward

Where a filing date falls on a Saturday, a Sunday or a statutory holiday, it is met on the next business day. The calculator shows every day skipped and names what closed it, which matters most around Christmas and Boxing Day, where two holidays and a weekend can sit together.

The Nine Days Treated as Holidays Here

HolidayWhen it falls
New Year’s DayJanuary 1
Family DayThird Monday in February
Good FridayTwo days before Easter Sunday
Victoria DayMonday on or before May 24
Canada DayJuly 1
Labour DayFirst Monday in September
ThanksgivingSecond Monday in October
Christmas DayDecember 25
Boxing DayDecember 26

These are the Ontario statutory holidays the deadline calculator already applies, so both tools agree about any date you put into them.

Where This Date Comes From

A T2 is due within six months of the fiscal year-end, and that is the date to put in here. The nil T2 deadline calculator works it out from a year-end and applies the shift itself, and the unfiled years checker lists it for every outstanding year at once.

A nil T2 is $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does the Shift Ever Move a Date Backwards?

No. A date on a closed day is met on the next business day, never an earlier one.

What Happens When Christmas Falls on a Friday?

December 25 closes the Friday, December 26 and the weekend follow, and the date lands on the Monday. Put the date in and the tool lists each day it skipped.

Are These Federal or Provincial Holidays?

They are the Ontario statutory holidays, which is what this firm files against. A corporation elsewhere may see a different local list, and the date the Canada Revenue Agency accepts is the one that matters.

Does the Shift Change How Many Days Late a Return Is?

It changes the date the return was due, so it changes the count from it. For a non-resident-owned corporation that count carries a charge, which the non-resident T2 penalty calculator works out.

Does Filing Early Ever Hurt?

No. The shift only matters at the end of the window. A nil return can be transmitted as soon as the tax year has ended.
